arguments.summary: Technical snapshot through split-adjusted SIP closes of 2026-09-18: ANET and META show the clearest positive 21/63-session relative trends; NVDA is positive but mixed versus XLK at 21 sessions; QQQ is short-term firm but trails at 63 sessions; MU has a sharp 21-session rebound after a negative, high-volatility 63-session period. These are completed-session observations, not forecasts or executable levels.

claims.text: ANET returned 6.94%/17.52% over 21/63 sessions, respectively, and exceeded SPY by 7.90/15.51 percentage points and XLK by 3.69/18.48 points. Its close was above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs, while 21/63-session realized volatility was 45.00%/57.14% and drawdown from the 252-session high was 5.28%.

QQQ returned 0.75% over 21 sessions but -2.59% over 63 sessions; it beat SPY by 1.71 points at 21 sessions but lagged by 4.59 points at 63, and lagged XLK at both horizons. The close remained above 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs; 21/63-session realized volatility was 13.19%/20.85% and 252-session-high drawdown was 3.31%.

MU gained 8.40% over 21 sessions and outperformed SPY/XLK by 9.36/5.15 points, but its 63-session return was -10.42%, lagging SPY/XLK by 12.42/9.46 points. It closed above all listed SMAs, but 21/63-session realized volatility was 52.49%/89.56% and drawdown from the 252-session high was 16.30%.

META was the strongest observed relative performer: its 21/63-session returns were 21.93%/15.34%, exceeding SPY by 22.88/13.34 points and XLC by 22.38/14.09 points. It closed above 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs, but RSI(14) was 77.87; 21/63-session realized volatility was 29.31%/44.80% and drawdown from the 252-session high was 14.67%.

NVDA returned 2.16%/5.50% over 21/63 sessions, exceeding SPY by 3.12/3.49 points; versus XLK it lagged by 1.08 points at 21 sessions but led by 6.46 points at 63. It closed above all listed SMAs, with 21/63-session realized volatility of 44.72%/39.63% and 5.71% drawdown from its 252-session high.

The evidence supports a narrow-leadership interpretation rather than broad risk confirmation: XLK rose over 21 sessions while IWM and HYG fell, and SPY was modestly negative. This qualifies extrapolation of the watchlist's relative strength.

gaps.description: The registered series provides 252-session summary indicators but no volume/liquidity statistics, intraday data, complete OHLC path, or longer history. Therefore support/resistance, volume confirmation, and trend persistence beyond the supplied SMA/ATR/RSI and return snapshots cannot be assessed.

assumptions: All reported returns are split-adjusted SIP price returns through the common 2026-09-18 close; they exclude distributions and are comparable only under that stated convention.
SMA-based thresholds below are review triggers based on completed closes, not support/resistance claims or execution instructions.
Realized volatility is backward-looking and is not an implied distribution or forecast.
arguments.counter_thesis: Momentum signals can fail if leadership broadens or reverses: SPY is near its 20/50-session averages while IWM and HYG are below theirs, and MU's recent rebound follows a negative, exceptionally volatile 63-session period. META's elevated RSI is descriptive rather than proof of reversal.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Technology-led relative performance is occurring alongside weak completed-session returns in IWM and HYG; the resulting narrow-leadership regime may increase common reversal risk among the watchlist's growth/technology-sensitive names.
shared_exposures.qualification: This is a market-regime inference from common-date price returns, not a measured correlation, portfolio exposure, or causal attribution.
